blocks.md: A **bearing** gives direction as an angle measured **clockwise from North**, with three figures: north is 000°, east 090°, south 180°, west 270°, and north-east 045°. To find the bearing from A to B, place the protractor at A, join to B and measure the angle clockwise from the north line. The **back bearing** (from B to A) is the bearing plus or minus 180°.

blocks.caption: Bearings from North
blocks.alt: A compass with bearings for north, east, south and west and a red arrow at 045 degrees.

blocks.title: Six-figure reference
blocks.md: A grid square is divided into **tenths** in each direction. Give the **easting** first: the two-figure line number then the tenths, and then the **northing**. For a point 5 tenths along from line 34 and 2 tenths up from line 27 the reference is **345 272**. Always: eastings (along) first, northings (up) second.

blocks.title: Distance and area
blocks.md:
- **Straight distance**: measure with a ruler and apply the scale.
- **Winding distance**: lay a thread or the edge of paper along the road, mark, then measure it against the scale.
- **Area**: count whole grid squares and combine part squares; if each square is 1 km × 1 km (1 km²), twelve squares make 12 km².

**Describing a place.** When asked to describe relief, drainage or settlement from a map, give evidence: quote contour heights, say where the land is steep or flat, name rivers and the direction they flow, describe roads, railways and settlement patterns, and mention land use symbols. Use grid references to point to places and compass directions to describe where things are.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Bearings are clockwise from north, never from east.
- The back bearing must stay between 000° and 360°: for 270° the back bearing is 090°.
- Do not give a six-figure reference with northing first.

blocks.title: Example 1: back bearing
blocks.statement: The bearing of a hill from a school is 060°. What is the bearing of the school from the hill?
steps: 240° is between 0° and 360°, so it is acceptable.

blocks.title: Example 2: area
blocks.statement: On a 1 km grid, a lake covers 7 whole squares and 6 half squares. Estimate its area.
steps: Half squares count as 3 whole squares (6 ÷ 2).
Each square is 1 km², so the area is 10 km².
